data.title: Nepal glacier saw exceptional heat before collapse caused deadly floods: researcher
data.description: PARIS - The mountain section whose collapse triggered fatal floods in Nepal and China on Aug 26 had experienced unprecedented heat for the time of year, meteorological data analysed by a researcher shows.

data.title: Ethiopia boosts drone production to fight rebels
data.description: ADDIS ABABA — Ethiopia has been manufacturing drones at two factories since last year and is now thought to have a fleet of thousands, analysts say, giving the government an edge against its multiple insurgent enemies.

data.title: Nepalis mark a year since deadly protests that toppled government
data.description: KATHMANDU - Dozens of young people congregated at Nepal’s burnt-out parliament building on Tuesday to mark the anniversary of deadly anti-corruption protests that toppled the former government.

data.title: Yemen rebel strikes on Saudi Arabia wound 73
data.description: RIYADH - Yemen's Houthi rebels struck a series of targets in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding 73, in their heaviest attack since the conflict reignited during the Middle East war.

data.title: North Korea hails Russia bridge as sign of tighter ties
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported Tuesday, as Pyongyang gains advantages from its powerful neighbours Moscow and Beijing.

data.title: Singapore proposes big salary hike for ministers
data.description: SINGAPORE - ⁠The Singapore government has accepted an independent committee’s recommendations for a sharp increase in ministerial ​salaries, which are already the highest ‌in the world, Prime ⁠Minister Lawrence Wong said on ​Tuesday.

data.title: Rubio launches Latin America tour to cement US influence
data.description: BARRANQUILLA (COLOMBIA) - United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrives in Colombia on Tuesday, the first stop on a Latin American tour designed to bolster pro-US leaders and cement influence over the continent.

data.title: Malaysian data centres guzzle more power as temperatures soar
data.description: KUALA ​LUMPUR - Malaysia's data centres are consuming more power ​as temperatures rise, leaving ‌a nine-gigawatt gas-fired capacity gap for the government to fill by 2032, officials said on Tuesday.

data.title: France tries 14 over deadliest Channel migrant crossing disaster
data.description: PARIS — Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.

data.title: Sweden heads to the polls in close election race
data.description: STOCKHOLM — Sweden votes Sunday in a tight general election that could see the left-wing opposition oust the government after a campaign dominated by concerns over healthcare and the welfare state amid fears over Europe's security.

data.title: Hong Kong customs seizes 200 crickets, 13kg of cockroaches at border checkpoint
data.description: Hong Kong customs officers have intercepted two travellers in separate cases at the Lo Wu border checkpoint for allegedly importing live insects commonly used as reptile feed.

data.title: Russia pummels Kyiv after three-day halt
data.description: KYIV - A wave of strong explosions rang out in Kyiv, Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) journalists said early Tuesday, as Russia resumed strikes on the Ukrainian capital after a three-day halt.

data.title: EXPLAINER - Why isn't oil above $100 despite supply disruptions?
data.description: SINGAPORE — Global oil benchmark ​Brent crude has rallied this month but stayed below US$100 a barrel despite recent escalation in the US-Iran conflict that has disrupted Gulf exports from the Strait of Hormuz and the ​Red Sea.

data.title: North Korea calls Russia bridge a sign of tighter ties
data.description: SEOUL — North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported Tuesday, as the Ukraine war draws the Western-sanctioned nations closer.

data.title: 'The ber months': Christmas arrives early in the Philippines
data.description: MANILA — At a city block-sized market in the Philippine capital, a platoon of plastic Santa Claus figures parachute from the ceiling of a shop already stacked high with Christmas decor despite the holiday being fully four months away.

data.title: US sanctions threaten to crush Iranian students' dreams
data.description: TEHRAN - She had planned to study psychology in Italy, but after US sanctions forced the suspension of an English exam required in order to make her dream come true, Iranian student Nikki cried for days.

data.title: Praying for rain as fires, haze plague Indonesian Borneo
data.description: PONTIANAK (INDONESIA) - Wildfires ravaging the Indonesian part of Borneo island are choking communities as far away as Malaysia with putrid haze, testing the resources and resolve of those having to endure them.

data.title: Indonesia reopens Jakarta airport, four others after Anak Krakatau ash clears
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesia ​has reopened its main Jakarta airport and four other airports ​that had been closed due ‌to volcanic ash from a series of eruptions at Mount Anak Krakatau, transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi said in a statement on Tuesday.

data.title: Panama Canal considering more cuts in transits due to El Nino
data.description: PANAMA CITY - The number of ships sailing through the Panama Canal could be cut further due to drought caused by the El Nino weather pattern, the new administrator of the waterway told AFP on Monday.

data.title: Flight data recorders recovered from Amazon cargo plane crash
data.description: MIAMI - Officials have recovered the flight data recorders from an Amazon cargo plane that overran the runway in Miami and slammed into two vehicles, killing five people, authorities said Monday.

data.title: US envoy sees 'movement' toward three-way talks with Russia, Ukraine
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A top US envoy on Monday touted progress in weekend discussions with Ukraine and Russia, raising the prospect of reviving three-way peace talks to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II.

data.title: Far-right victory in Germany draws protesters in Berlin
data.description: BERLIN - Several thousand protesters gathered at Berlin's Brandenburg Gate Monday to decry the far-right Alterantive for Germany (AfD) after the party scored a breakthrough victory in a regional election the previous day.

data.title: UK PM denounces 'politics of poison' after anti-migrant protests
data.description: LONDON - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged his Labour Party lawmakers to stop the "politics of poison seeping into our streets" after demonstrators tried to block the arrival of migrants, a media report said Monday.

data.title: Eiffel Tower closed in row over women removed for Hindu group
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday because of a strike by staff over the removal of female colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group, workers and management said.

data.title: Lebanon says 12 killed in strikes as Israel vows to 'remove threats'
data.description: KFAR RUMMAN, Lebanon - Israel conducted a wave of airstrikes in south Lebanon, killing 12 people including women and children according to the Lebanese health ministry on Monday, in an intensification of violence after a weeks-long lull.

data.title: Israeli rubble-clearing in Gaza could erase 'atrocity crimes' evidence
data.description: GENEVA — An expert of the United Nations (UN) warned Monday that large-scale rubble removal in parts of Gaza under Israeli control risked erasing traces of "atrocity crimes", and preventing the recovery and identification of human remains.

data.title: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 jobs as European car sector hits skids
data.description: LONDON - Jaguar Land Rover said Monday that it would cut "around 4,000 roles over the next two years", or about ten percent of its global workforce, in a further blow to Europe's automobile industry.

data.title: Nepal holds day of mourning as families pray missing still alive
data.description: KATHMANDU (NEPAL) - Nepal held a national day of mourning Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive.

data.title: Germany's Merz under pressure from far-right election triumph
data.description: BERLIN - German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will huddle Monday with his CDU party to discuss and digest their thumping defeat at the hands of the far-right AfD party in a state election in the ex-communist east.

data.title: Nepal tunnel rescues face 'unprecedented' challenge
data.description: KATHMANDU (NEPAL) - Nepal's flood disaster posed an unprecedented challenge, Australian rescue expert Arnold Dix said Monday, with multiple search operations underway in Himalayan hydropower tunnels.

data.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
data.description: JAKARTA - Jakarta's main airport and three others delayed reopening on Monday after halting operations due to a volcanic eruption and leaving hundreds of thousands stranded.

data.title: AI data centers are less thirsty now, tech giants say
data.description: NEW YORK - Data centers are running into a wall of public anger in the United States over their thirst for water and power.

data.title: North Korea vows nuclear-armed navy as US ally drills open
data.description: SEOUL - Leader Kim Jong Un vowed to build North Korea's navy into a nuclear-armed force, state media reported Monday as US allies' maritime drills were to begin.

data.title: 'Trumpapalooza' tests Republican bet on unpopular US president
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US Republicans will gather in Dallas, Texas, next week for a two-day convention aimed at convincing voters that Donald Trump is effectively on the ballot in November -- even as the deeply unpopular president threatens to become a liability for his own party.

data.title: 25 years on, America seeks to keep 9/11 memories alive
data.description: NEW YORK - A quarter century after the era-defining attacks of September 11, the United States is eager to keep alive the memory of a 2001 trauma that is fading as the proportion of Americans who did not experience it firsthand grows.
